problems.statement: The zero-deviation record is an artifact of the Feb 2026 supervisor bonus penalty, which suppressed deviation reporting; it does not reflect real quality improvement.
Line 3 is not a superior line: its 118% attainment is explained by 4-7 borrowed technicians per day from Lines 1 and 4 charged to home lines, and its per-technician-hour productivity is unchanged.

Line 3 is hiding defects through off-record rework (unrecorded re-bonding in the back cage, not in the device history record), which is a probable data-integrity and regulatory compliance breach; allegation is single-source anonymous but corroborated by circumstantial evidence.

The Quality Manager's claim that the first-pass quality training program caused the deviation drop is rejected: the drop preceded the program launch (Feb vs 9 Mar) and completion was only 40% by June.

The Line 3 supervisor's explanation (5S and huddles, early problem catching) is rejected as the cause of Line 3's performance, since huddles predate the change and productivity per technician-hour is flat.
The new lower-cost tubing supplier explains the leaks and extra purchases.
The underlying luer-bond process problem (cure-time variability at Line 3 bonding) was never fixed (CAPA open, no change control), so the defects persist and are now hidden rather than eliminated.

Governance and escalation have failed: the ethics case was closed by the Plant Manager, who authored the incentive, with no investigation; leadership is conflicted and the plant has a speak-up climate problem.

causalClaims.to: Rising customer complaints (luer leaks) and higher final-inspection rejections

actions.action: Decline to document Line 3 as a template or roll it out to other lines.
actions.rationale: The apparent Line 3 advantage is borrowed labor and probably masked rework, so copying it would spread the problem.

actions.action: Suspend or rescind the per-deviation supervisor bonus deduction and replace it with incentives that reward reporting and detection.
actions.rationale: It is the identified driver of suppressed reporting, and it can be reversed cheaply.

actions.action: Reopen the ethics case under independent investigators (corporate or quality/regulatory) outside the Plant Manager: records review, back-cage walk-through, device history record vs purchasing reconciliation, protected interviews.
actions.rationale: The prior closure was conflicted and had no evidence gathering, and a possible undocumented rework could be a regulatory breach.

actions.action: Quarantine and risk-assess suspect Line 3 lots and assess customer notification and regulatory reporting obligations if off-record rework is confirmed.
actions.rationale: Leaking infusion sets are a patient-safety risk and complaints are rising.

actions.action: Close CAPA-2025-117 by fixing the luer bonding cure-time variability across stations.
actions.rationale: The real technical root defect remains unaddressed.

actions.action: Reconcile resource attribution and stop unrecorded labor lending; correct line-level performance data and purchases by line.
actions.rationale: Accurate data is needed to evaluate lines but is secondary to safety and integrity.

actions.action: Punish or discipline the Line 3 supervisor or technicians now.
actions.rationale: Rework allegation is unconfirmed and the incentive design created the pressure; punishment before investigation would chill reporting further.

actions.action: Expand the first-pass quality training as the fix.
actions.rationale: Training did not cause the drop and does not address the incentive and reporting problem.

actions.action: Treat the zero-deviation record and the nine-month streak as a basis for customer or board claims.
actions.rationale: The metric is invalid and contradicted by complaints and QC rejections.

nextEvidence: Direct inspection of the Line 3 back cage plus device history records, connector and adhesive consumption, and rework logs against purchasing by line
Protected interviews with Line 3 second-shift technicians and borrowed technicians, and the source of the lending instruction to Line 4
Lot-level traceability of complaint and rejected lots to line, shift and bonding station with cure-time data, plus the rationale for CAPA-2025-117 remaining open
output.summary: The zero-deviation streak and Line 3 template are artifacts, not performance. The February 2026 bonus penalty for each deviation suppressed reporting, with deviations collapsing before training began. Line 3's 118% comes from 4-7 borrowed technicians charged to other lines; productivity per hour is flat. Complaints (11 to 31 ppm, mostly Line 3 luer leaks), QC rejections, and 30% higher component purchases point to hidden rework, alleged by the hotline and closed without investigation by the conflicted Plant Manager. CAPA-2025-117 is still unfixed. Don't roll out Line 3; remove the penalty, independently investigate, assess product risk, fix the bonding process.
